fieldMarks: Male mostly gray with a contrasting black stern; looks plain at a distance
Female mottled brown with a gray-and-orange bill
Steeper forehead than a female mallard
Square white patch on the trailing edge of the wing, obvious in flight
behavior: Dabbles while swimming, taking more leaves and stems of aquatic plants than other dabblers; seldom forages on land
Migrates in flocks but is not a long-distance migrant; most winter north of the tropics
Primary migration corridor runs from the prairies south through the central plains
habitat: Summers around fresh or alkaline lakes in open prairie and intermountain valleys, locally coastal marshes; in migration and winter on marshes, lakes and estuaries, generally not salt water.
range: Breeds from southern Alaska, southern Yukon and the southern Mackenzie across the Prairie Provinces to southern Ontario, southwestern Quebec and the Maritimes, south to the southwestern and central United States; most common on inland waters west of the Mississippi.
